request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have dates and a person can have several, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it behaves now**
- **Adding a hold:** each person's row has a from-date field, an optional to-date field and a Hold button. A blank from-date uses the sheet's today. A blank to-date means the hold never ends.
- **Listing holds:** every hold the person has is shown in the row. "Hold yes/no" means the person has at least one hold.
- **Refusals:** a date that isn't a real yyyy-mm-dd date, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused with the usual error message and nothing is stored.
- **Audit:** holding writes `PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>`. There is no release action any more, so `PERSON_RELEASED` is gone; a hold ends on its to-date.
- **What a hold leaves out:** only open claims dated inside a hold are dropped from the live totals. That applies to the person's own totals, the sheet's totals and period totals. A claim bound by a statement still counts whatever its date. A statement taken during a hold doesn't bind the claims the hold leaves out. The server and the screen both use this same rule.

**Two choices you might want to change**
- **Pending claims:** "bound by a statement" excludes pending claims, because the app already treats a pending claim as not bound until it is approved or rejected. So a pending claim inside a hold is left out even if a statement covered it.
- **Old data:** the migration (`V25__person_hold.sql`) moves holds into a new `person_hold` table and removes the old `held` column. Anyone held before this change gets an open-ended hold from the beginning of time, so their totals don't change.

**Where the changes are**
- **Server:** the hold endpoint `hold.PUT.yml` has a new first step, `ValidateHold`. `HoldPerson` now adds a hold instead of toggling one. There is a new `Hold` record, and `Person` now carries a list of holds instead of a yes/no flag. The rule itself is `Rollup.counts`, which `TakeStatement` also uses.
- **Front end:** the hold cell is in `hold.slot.tsx`. `peopleQuery.ts` gets the list of holds and a `heldOn` helper, and `claimsQuery.ts` applies the rule on the screen.
